transcript.content: Hello, please have a seat. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, I'm here because my wife actually suggested it. What finally made me agree to come in is that I just... I don't care about the things that used to keep me balanced. I used to do sailing races, I had a Saturday shift at the historical society, I'd tinker in my woodshop. But lately, all of that just feels like chores. I keep putting them off. I just don't have the interest anymore.
About how long have you been feeling this loss of interest?
Well, it's been going on since the scaffold accident... that happened during the business readjustment at work. So, I'd say it's been a little over a year now.
Were you physically injured during the scaffold accident?
No, I wasn't. I mean, physically, I didn't get hurt at all. I just... walked away without a scratch, really.
Since the accident, have you experienced any unwanted memories, flashbacks, or nightmares about what happened?

Yeah, I do. Sometimes, just out of nowhere, I'll see that scaffold dropping in my head. It's... it's clear as a photo. It really happens if I hear a loud metal clank, or like a backup alarm on a truck outside. And when it happens, for a few minutes, it's just really hard to stay focused on whatever meeting or conversation I'm actually in at the time.
Do you find yourself trying to avoid places, people, or conversations that remind you of the accident?

Yeah, I do. I've actually gotten very good at routing my day so I don't have to go anywhere near that coastal site, or even the harbor walkways by the cranes. And at work, if I end up in a conversation where someone starts replaying what went wrong that day... I just steer clear or find a reason to leave. It's just easier to avoid it.
Since the accident, have you found yourself feeling constantly on guard, or more easily startled than you used to be?

Yeah, I have. I mean, especially with sudden noises. If... if someone drops a metal ladder, or a truck gate slams, I jump hard before I can even stop myself. And then it just takes me a lot longer than it really should to get my heart rate back down to normal.
